RagShortTexts: The Battle of the Aegates Islands (241 BC) saw Rome decisively defeat Carthage's fleet, ending the First Punic War with the cession of Sicily.

Variants.Content: Bankrupt after disastrous storms, Rome's patriotic citizens privately funded a new fleet of 200 streamlined quinqueremes commanded by Consul Gaius Lutatius Catulus. On March 10, 241 BC, off the western tip of Sicily at the Aegates Islands, Catulus intercepted Carthage's fleet laden with provisions under Hanno. Laden and undermanned, the Carthaginian ships were routed: 50 were sunk and 70 captured. With Hamilcar Barca's army isolated on Sicily and the treasury drained, Carthage sued for peace. Under the Treaty of Lutatius, Carthage evacuated Sicily and adjacent isles and agreed to pay 3,200 silver talents over ten years, concluding the 23-year war.

The Aegates Islands proved the unmatched civic sacrifice of Rome! When the treasury lay barren, private citizens financed the galleys that secured our triumph. Catulus attacked through adverse gales, shattering the lumbering Punic transports. With their lifeline severed, even Hamilcar was forced to capitulate!

Aegates was an administrative failure that cost us an empire. Hamilcar remained unvanquished upon Mount Eryx, yet the Council of 104 dispatched an overloaded, untrained supply armada to slaughter. We surrendered fertile Sicily and emptied our vaults to pay Rome's extortion, lighting the fuse of the Mercenary War.
